title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Competitive Methods - Multi-step bidding
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: In a Multi-step Invitation for Bids, what is strictly evaluated during the first phase of the process?
questions.explain: In multi-step bidding, the first step evaluates unpriced technical proposals to determine which bidders are qualified. Only those deemed technically acceptable are permitted to submit priced bids in the second step.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: In a two-step competitive sealed bidding process, which vendors are invited to submit sealed financial pricing in Step Two?
options: All vendors who downloaded the solicitation in Step One
Only the vendor who ranked highest in technical qualifications
Any vendor whose unpriced technical offer was determined acceptable in Step One
Only those vendors who can prove local small business certification
questions.explain: Two-step IFBs invite unpriced technical proposals first. Only the vendors who pass the technical threshold (determined acceptable) are allowed to submit sealed pricing in the second phase.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: When is a multi-step bidding process most advantageous for an agency?
options: When the agency needs office supplies delivered overnight
When specifications are inadequate to permit a standard IFB, but price will still be the final determining factor among qualified designs
When purchasing strictly A&E consulting services
When an emergency is declared and competition is suspended
questions.explain: Multi-step bidding is ideal when the agency knows what it needs but doesn't have specifications rigid enough for a standard IFB. It allows the agency to accept diverse technical solutions in step 1, then use price as the final deciding factor in step 2 among acceptable solutions.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: During Step One of a multi-step IFB, technical proposals are received. How are these proposals categorized by the procurement team?
options: Scored on a scale of 1 to 100
Lowest price, median price, or highest price
questions.explain: In a multi-step IFB, Step One does not involve scoring numerical weights. Proposals are evaluated on a pass/fail basis as acceptable, potentially acceptable (needing clarification), or unacceptable.
